attacks.claim: A provider outage or 10DLC filtering sends every SMS to failed status. Two failures per patron then permanently switch that patron to NOTICE_PREV, with no circuit breaker or fallback-only-without-switch. Phone-channel patrons would flip to ~$0.11 calls (about $2,250 for the assumed 20,500 phone uptake) and lose their SMS preference silently.
attacks.evidence: "After 2 consecutive failures it switches the patron back to `NOTICE_PREV` and adds a staff note to verify the number."

attacks.claim: After CallNotify ends (2027-03-31), phone is no longer a valid channel, yet NOTICE_PREV is set to `phone` for new sign-ups and the STOP and failure paths route back to it. Notices queued to phone after that date are silently lost, which violates the agreed 'no patron may lose hold notices' constraint. LIBSYS-330 is out of scope and undefined. The rollback claim is also false: new sign-ups had no prior channel, so they would be moved to a channel they never had.
attacks.evidence: "(new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`; every SMS patron has a mobile number)" vs "Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before." and "CallNotify contract ends 2027-03-31 and will not be renewed"

attacks.claim: The $600/month approved cap has no enforcement. The only control is an alert at $450 that triggers no action. Uptake is an unsourced assumption, and at about 52,800 texts/month (1.7x the assumed 30,500) spend exceeds the cap with nothing stopping it. Provider billing lag makes this worse.
attacks.evidence: "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons ≈ 30,500 texts/month." and "a provider spend alert fires at $450."

attacks.claim: The stated guarantee that STOP senders are never re-texted depends on an opt-out record that the described data model never writes. The STOP handler only changes transport preferences and adds a circulation note, and SMS_CONSENT is not updated. Protection rests entirely on a provider-side block that is per-number and can be cleared or reassigned.
attacks.evidence: "Consent and opt-out records are kept, so re-enabling later never texts anyone who sent STOP."

attacks.claim: The week-3 staff pilot sends live texts. If 10DLC approval slips past week 3 (1–3 weeks from Oct 20), the pilot is unregistered A2P traffic that carriers may filter, and its delivery metrics would be invalid.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in; we verify delivery" vs "Public launch is gated on approval."

attacks.claim: A new public-facing webhook runs on the Koha app host with DB write credentials. The signature scheme, body size limits and parameterization are unspecified. The dedicated user also has no SELECT grant, yet phone-number matching requires reads, so the grant list is incomplete or reads are happening through a broader account.
attacks.evidence: "The receiver uses a dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`."

attacks.claim: The provider and carriers retain phone numbers and 90-day delivery metadata linking a phone to library hold-ready events, and the template exposes branch and item count. The statute covers materials, so this is probably compliant, but linkability is not analyzed.
attacks.evidence: "delivery metadata is kept 90 days per contract."

attacks.claim: The claim that switching providers is only a config change is contradicted by the provider-specific webhook (signature verification, payload handling), provider-side STOP/HELP configuration and provider 10DLC registration. Exit cost is understated.
attacks.evidence: "Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change." vs "A webhook receiver (~150 lines ...) ... verifies the provider's request signature"

attacks.claim: The cost model assumes one GSM-7 segment per text at a flat $0.011. The Spanish template with accented characters would likely be UCS-2 and split into multiple segments, with no segment accounting for that share.
attacks.evidence: "Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment"

attacks.claim: Rollback is a one-shot mass update of every SMS patron, tested only on a staging copy with no production dry-run or idempotency described. Re-queuing pending SMS rows on the restored channel may also duplicate notices already queued by the failure fallback.
attacks.evidence: "`sms_rollback.pl`, written and tested in week 2 against a staging copy of the patron database"

attacks.claim: The 9.2%-to-5.5% expiry target is a causal claim with no control group. SMS self-selects, and the 50%/10% uptake and 64% survey preference (a stated preference, not behaviour) are unprototyped.
attacks.evidence: "Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5% (phone today: 9.2%)."

attacks.claim: The enrolment confirmation and STOP/HELP copy are English-only for Spanish-preferring patrons, and no native-speaker review of the Spanish template is described.
attacks.evidence: "On enrolment, Koha sends one confirmation text: \"Riverbend Library: you'll get a text...\""

attacks.claim: One developer must deliver a webhook receiver, en/es templates, a rollback script, a desk procedure, a staff guide and a pilot in four weeks, which is tight and leaves little room for the failure-path testing the plan relies on.
attacks.evidence: "Team: library systems developer (1), circulation lead (0.5) · 4 weeks"

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy: the 15-minute queue cadence and volume (~141k notices/month) are well within range. Phone-number lookups for STOP fan-out lack a stated index, which is non-blocking.
Nothing gate-worthy beyond the Spanish segment-length issue above.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no rendering or layout concerns in an SMS-only plan

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy: the plan targets a measured preference and an expiry gap.
attacks.evidence: "64% of phone-notice patrons would prefer a text message."

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy: opt-in is one OPAC step or one desk step.
attacks.evidence: "Patrons choose SMS in the OPAC under \"Your messaging\", or staff set it at the desk"

attacks.claim: Nothing further gate-worthy beyond the items above.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no additional gate-worthy issues found
